clue.text: Keep an eye on the dog, perhaps

definitions.meaning: one of the short duty periods on board ship, so it is an example of a turn of duty

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep an eye on the family dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The dog' is not the animal: aboard ship the dog watches are the two short evening duty spells.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe attentively is the verb sense; a shipboard duty spell such as the dog is the noun sense.

clue.text: How market stallholders are equipped to resist

definitions.meaning: traders at a market come provided with a stall, read here as a phrase

explanation.surface: Market traders are well prepared to hold out.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer describes a trader who has a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out against pressure is to resist it; the split phrase means having a stall.

clue.text: Where lived the brave, put finally to the sword

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of the word put

parts.note: an épée is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: Where a warrior lived was put to the sword in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is a noun: a Native American warrior, whose dwelling is this conical tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is the conical tent used by Plains peoples of North America.

clue.text: I lost out, surrounded by damage in bad weather

indicators.note: surrounded by means the rearranged letters sit within the word for damage

parts.note: harm means damage

indicators.note: out signals the letters of I lost are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone lost out, ringed by destruction in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' is the anagram signal for I LOST; 'surrounded by' puts the result inside the word for damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm of falling ice pellets is a type of bad weather.

clue.text: Sack Mark, a trouble-maker

parts.note: to sack someone is to dismiss them from a job, to fire them
a brand is a mark burnt or stamped on something

explanation.surface: A man called Mark is dismissed for stirring up trouble at work.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator who stirs up unrest is called a firebrand, like a burning torch spreading flames.

clue.text: Charge for transporting soldiers into battle

indicators.note: into means the soldiers go inside the word for battle

parts.note: a fight is a battle
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Soldiers are charged as they are transported into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is the fee paid for carrying goods, as well as the goods themselves.

clue.text: One standing by book

definitions.meaning: a substitute waiting to step in
to book is to make an advance booking

explanation.definitionFit: A substitute player is one waiting in the wings; to book a table is to secure it in advance.

clue.text: Half-back stands on anyone in wet ground

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word back is its first two letters

parts.note: you can mean anyone, as in you never know

explanation.surface: A rugby half-back stands over someone on a muddy pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer BA 'stands on' YOU, sitting above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayou is a marshy creek or swamp in the southern US.

clue.text: Monk gets up to admit brothers and one divine

indicators.note: to admit means to take the others inside
gets up in a down answer means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist monk of Tibet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A monk rises to let in his brothers and a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'gets up' reads the monk upwards; 'to admit' takes in the brothers and one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosial means fit for the gods, heavenly in taste or scent.

clue.text: Refuse doctor nothing on ship

parts.note: O is the zero digit, nothing
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A doctor declines to go on board with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the noun (rubbish), not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless waste matter, rubbish.

clue.text: Intoxication upsets one head

parts.note: upsets as a verb means tips over
I is the Roman numeral for one
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Inverness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Drunkenness unsettles a person's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsets' looks like an anagram signal but simply means TIPS. A NESS is a promontory, a head of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsiness is mild drunkenness, a state of being somewhat drunk.

clue.text: Booby, to put it another way

definitions.text: Booby, to put it another way

indicators.note: saying the word differently here means its letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A fool is called by a different name.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: a rearrangement of the letters of 'Booby' gives another word for a loutish fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby is a stupid person and a yobbo is a loutish oaf, so one coarse term restates the other.

clue.text: Spots, so to speak, before the eyes

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word is to be heard rather than written

parts.note: specks are small spots or dots

explanation.surface: Someone sees spots floating before their eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a vision problem, but glasses are what sit before the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles, informally glasses, are worn in front of a person's eyes.

clue.text: What extraordinarily oral gurus are

indicators.note: extraordinarily suggests the letters of oral gurus are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A description of spiritual teachers who talk an unusual amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinarily' rearranges ORALGURUS; the whole clue also describes talkative gurus.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers who talk a great deal are loquacious, excessively chatty.

clue.text: A slight reverse half face-to-face

indicators.note: reverse means those two letters are read backwards
half of the four-letter word face is its first two letters

parts.note: front means face, as the front of a building is its face

explanation.surface: A small setback when meeting someone in person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes FA from the first 'face' and 'reverse' turns it to AF; the second 'face' gives FRONT, with 'to' joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is an insult, a deliberate show of disrespect.

clue.text: As of old, be unfolds a story

indicators.note: unfolds means the letters are opened out into a new order

parts.note: the printed words, with be standing for the setter's intended he

explanation.surface: In the old way, someone tells a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfolds' rearranges AS OF OLD HE; the print has 'be', which lacks the H, so the setter's word must have been 'he'.
explanation.definitionFit: A story in the colloquial sense is a fib, an untruth.

clue.text: Rose at Granichester thus unofficially gives tongue

definitions.meaning: Rupert Brooke's poem about Grantchester, near Cambridge, describes an unofficial rose of the national kind growing in its hedges

explanation.surface: A rose growing in a Cambridgeshire village speaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Brooke's 'The Old Vicarage, Grantchester' has the line 'An English unofficial rose'. The page prints Granichester, a slip for Grantchester.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of England is a tongue; the rose in Brooke's poem is called that national kind, unofficial.

clue.text: Garment of angora, perhaps, worn by soldiers and young airmen

indicators.note: worn by means the soldiers and cadets sit within the animal, carrying it as clothing

parts.note: the angora is a breed of goat
RE is the Royal Engineers
ATC is the Air Training Corps, the RAF's youth cadet organisation

explanation.surface: Soldiers and air cadets wear a garment made of angora wool.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angora is a goat breed as well as a wool, so 'angora, perhaps' names the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy overcoat, especially one issued to soldiers, is this long coat.

clue.text: Central heating system developed thus without an imitation arising

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so those letters enclose the other piece
developed means the letters of thus take a new shape
arising in a down answer means the piece is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a copy is an imitation

explanation.surface: A heating system was developed without anything arising from imitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense of outside, not 'lacking'; 'developed' is the anagram signal and 'arising' reverses in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypocaust is the Roman underfloor heating system, hot air circulating beneath the floor.

clue.text: Difficult decision I had, on reflection, left to Miss Woodhouse

indicators.note: reflection is a mirror image, so the shortened form is read backwards

parts.note: I had shortens to I'd
Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel Emma

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a hard choice that was left to Jane Austen's heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' sounds like thinking it over, but it turns ID into DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a quandary, a situation needing a choice between awkward options.

clue.text: What durables are, and a big noise therein

indicators.note: therein means the noise sits inside the two words a big

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Lasting goods carry a lot of noise inside them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Therein' puts DIN inside A BIG: A-BI-DIN-G.
explanation.definitionFit: Durable goods are lasting, built to endure.

clue.text: More than cover remaining drink

parts.note: over means left or remaining, as in food left over
to lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone wants more than the cover charge for the drink left over.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlap is to extend beyond and partly cover something else.

clue.text: Differing with M.O., I play games here

indicators.note: differing means the letters take a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone with a different method plays games here.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of MO I PLAY give the site in Greece of the ancient Olympic Games.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia in Greece was the site of the ancient Olympic Games.

clue.text: Early development of city district during Cypriot revolution

indicators.note: during means the district sits inside the rearranged letters
revolution means the letters of Cypriot are turned over into a new order

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: A city district grew up early during an uprising in Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' is the anagram signal; 'during' puts the City of London postcode inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Precocity is the quality of maturing or showing ability unusually young.

clue.text: Magazine making a hit

definitions.meaning: the long-running British humorous weekly magazine

explanation.surface: A magazine becomes a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a famous British satirical weekly, published 1841 to 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: The satirical weekly shared its name with a blow with the fist.

clue.text: The conclusion of a home game

indicators.note: of signals the answer is taken out of the run of letters a home game

explanation.surface: The end of a home match.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'hOME GAme'.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end.

clue.text: Subject to very good conditions initially

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good in a moral sense

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word conditions

explanation.surface: Something offered subject to very good terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to' looks like a phrase but 'Subject' alone is the definition; 'to' gives its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: She passes depression on to father

parts.note: the pip is an old British phrase for a fit of low spirits
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A woman passes her low spirits on to her dad.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning's verse drama 'Pippa Passes' gives the definition. 'The pip' is dated British slang for a bout of low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning's poetic drama is titled after its heroine, the silk-winder who goes past.

clue.text: One in black going round being tearful

indicators.note: going round means the whole result is turned around and read backwards
in places one letter inside the word for black

parts.note: ebon is a poetic word for black, as in ebony
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in black is going about in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into EBON to give EBOIN, and 'going round' turns that to the answer. In Greek myth Niobe wept endlessly for her slain children.
explanation.definitionFit: Niobe, who turned to a weeping stone after losing her children, is the classic figure of a person in tears.

clue.text: Off the cuff. I am to remind you while speaking

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
to prompt someone is to remind them of their lines

indicators.note: while speaking signals the word is heard rather than spelt, so it becomes a single letter

parts.note: you is the word said, written as the letter that has the same sound

explanation.surface: Someone talking says they will jog another person's memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is improvised, done without preparation.

clue.text: Inside the park, called a shrub

indicators.note: inside means one word sits within the other

parts.note: Hyde Park is London's best-known park
rang means telephoned or called

explanation.surface: Someone called from inside the park about a shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The park' is London's Hyde Park, the most famous park for a British solver.
explanation.definitionFit: The hydrangea is a flowering garden bush with large rounded heads of blooms.

clue.text: Food and drink

definitions.meaning: to raise a glass in honour of someone

explanation.definitionFit: Grilled bread is something to eat, and drinking to someone's health is the verb sense.
